result.rationale: The diff shows `minimumTokenResponseSchema` with computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`, which evaluate to a fixed literal string (ZodType's toString output), not a catch-all for arbitrary properties. Real token refresh payloads (expiry_date, refresh_token, etc.) won't have that literal key, so `safeParse(response)` in parseRefreshTokenResponse fails and the function throws 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned' whenever APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is on — breaking token refresh for Google/Zoom/Office365/Salesforce as wired up in this diff. Mechan

judged_text: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed object keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`, which evaluate to the literal string produced by ZodType's toString (e.g. '[object Object]'), not 'any property'. When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is on, every credential sync token refresh fails safeParse (real payloads have keys like expiry_date, not the literal garbage key) and the function throws 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned', breaking Google/Zoom/Office365/Salesforce token refresh entirely for self-hosters who enable the feature.
